```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(PGViS)
set.seed(1)
```

The final step turns per-variant metrics into one number per patient: the
cumulative PGViS score. This vignette runs end to end on the fixture.

## From variants to samples

A variant is carried by some set of samples. To score samples, we first expand
each variant into one row per carrier, then average the metrics within each
sample.

```{r explode}
metrics <- pgvis_variant_metrics(pgvis_example("variants"),
                                 pgvis_example("predictions"))
metrics <- pgvis_filter_disruptive(metrics, ref_prob_min = 0.5,
                                   alt_prob_max = 0.5, min_carrier_frac = 0)

long <- pgvis_explode_carriers(metrics)
nrow(metrics)
nrow(long)          # one row per (variant, carrier)
```

Attach ancestry (needed for the standardisation, explained below), then
aggregate:

```{r aggregate}
clin <- pgvis_example("clinical")
clin$superpopulation <- pgvis_map_superpopulation(clin$race)
long <- dplyr::left_join(long, clin[, c("sample", "superpopulation")],
                         by = "sample")

per_sample <- pgvis_aggregate_samples(long)
per_sample <- per_sample[!is.na(per_sample$superpopulation), ]
head(per_sample)
```

Self-reported race maps to a 1000 Genomes superpopulation; anything that
doesn't map becomes `NA` and those samples are excluded rather than pooled
into a default group. Where you have genotype-inferred ancestry, prefer it.

## Scoring against a reference

The score is defined relative to a reference cohort — typically the
1000 Genomes panel, run through the identical pipeline. Here we synthesise a
reference arm so the vignette can score end to end:

```{r panel}
ped <- pgvis_load_pedigree(
  system.file("extdata", "toy_pedigree.txt", package = "PGViS"))

panel <- data.frame(
  sample = ped$sample, superpopulation = ped$superpopulation,
  cohort = "1000Genomes", n_variants = 10L,
  delta_wi_int   = rnorm(nrow(ped)),
  log_odds_ratio = rnorm(nrow(ped)),
  delta_af_alt   = rnorm(nrow(ped))
)

stacked <- pgvis_bind_panel(per_sample, panel)
```

`pgvis_bind_panel()` refuses to proceed if the cohort and reference share no
superpopulation — which would otherwise produce a table of all-`NA` z-scores
instead of an error.

## The composite

```{r score}
scored <- pgvis_score(stacked, reference_group = "1000Genomes")
head(scored[, c("sample", "cohort", "superpopulation", "pgvis")])
```

Three things happen inside:

1. **Robust standardisation.** Each metric is centred on the median and scaled
   by the MAD *of the reference cohort within the same superpopulation*.
   Median/MAD rather than mean/SD because the metric distributions have heavy
   tails.
2. **Weighting.** The weights are the absolute PC1 loadings of the scaled
   z-scores, normalised to sum to one — each metric weighted by how much it
   contributes to the shared signal, not by a hand-picked constant.
3. **Combination.** The score is the weighted sum.

```{r weights}
attr(scored, "weights")
```

### Why ancestry matching is not optional

Allele-frequency divergence from a reference panel scales with how genetically
distant a sample is from that panel. Standardise against the whole panel and
the score largely reports ancestry. Standardising *within* superpopulation
removes that confound. `pgvis_score(strata = NULL)` exists for a genuinely
homogeneous cohort and is the wrong choice otherwise.

### Freeze the weights for validation

The weights are refit from PC1 by default, so two runs aren't on the same
scale unless you say so. When you score a validation cohort, reuse the
discovery weights:

```{r frozen}
w  <- attr(scored, "weights")
s2 <- pgvis_score(stacked, weights = w)      # same scale as `scored`
identical(attr(s2, "weights"), w)
```

## Comparing groups

`pgvis_compare_groups()` gives ROC AUC, Cohen's d and a permutation p-value —
and withholds them when a group is too small to interpret.

```{r compare}
demo <- data.frame(pgvis = c(rnorm(120, 0), rnorm(120, 1.1)),
                   group = rep(c("control", "case"), each = 120))
pgvis_compare_groups(demo, min_n = 50, n_perm = 500)[,
  c("n1", "n2", "auc", "cohens_d", "perm_p")]
```

Below `min_n` per group it returns `valid = FALSE` and a label saying so,
rather than a confident effect size from a dozen samples. The permutation
p-value uses the add-one estimator, so it's never reported as exactly zero.

## Survival

Downstream, but common enough to wrap. It runs a log-rank test across score
groups and a Cox model on the continuous score, supports covariates so you can
check the score isn't just reporting stage, and refuses non-binary event
coding.

```{r survival}
n <- 300
score <- rnorm(n)
time  <- rexp(n, rate = exp(0.7 * score) / 500)   # higher score, shorter time
sc  <- data.frame(sample = paste0("S", 1:n), pgvis = score)
cl  <- data.frame(sample = paste0("S", 1:n), time = time,
                  event = rbinom(n, 1, 0.8))

res <- pgvis_survival(sc, cl)
res$summary
```

`pgvis_plot_survival(res)` draws the Kaplan-Meier curves (with a risk table if
`survminer` is installed, base graphics otherwise).

## Provenance

`pgvis_run()` — the one-call wrapper for this whole R-side sequence — writes a
manifest next to the results recording the thresholds, the derived weights,
input row counts and any QC warnings. Months later, when you need to know
exactly which settings produced a given table, the answer is sitting next to
it rather than lost to memory.

```{r run, eval = FALSE}
res <- pgvis_run(cfg, variants, clinical = clin,
                 reference_group = "1000Genomes")
```

## What can go wrong

- **Reference group absent.** The score is defined relative to a reference; if
  `reference_group` isn't in the data, `pgvis_score()` stops rather than
  standardising against nothing.
- **Zero MAD in a stratum.** If a metric is constant within a reference
  stratum the z-score is undefined; PGViS falls back to the SD there and warns.
- **Comparing scores across runs.** Only valid if the weights are frozen. Two
  independently-fit runs are not on the same scale.

That's the whole pipeline. The [overview](PGViS.html) has the condensed
version, and [the cluster guide](pipeline.html) has the shell side in one
place.
